title: Bounded ambient base change for integral stratum extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$, and all arrows are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. On their small pro-étale sites put $R_V=\mathcal O_{E,V}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use module pullback and its composition maps [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], applied termwise to bounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and open extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek].

Let $h:T'\to T$, let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be open with closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$, and form their fibre products $j':U'\hookrightarrow T'$ and $i':Z'\hookrightarrow T'$, with projections $h_U:U'\to U$ and $h_Z:Z'\to Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every $N\in D^b(U,R_U)$ the map
$$\beta_N:j'_!h_U^*N\longrightarrow h^*j_!N$$
adjoint to $h_U^*N\cong j'^*h^*j_!N$, using the open adjunction unit and pullback composition, is an isomorphism. For every $N\in D^b(Z,R_Z)$ the map
$$\gamma_N:h^*i_*N\longrightarrow i'_*h_Z^*N$$
is an isomorphism; it is the closed adjunction unit followed by $i'^*h^*i_*N\cong h_Z^*N$. Under the canonical identifications, $j'^*\beta_N$ and $i'^*\gamma_N$ are identities, while $i'^*\beta_N$ and $j'^*\gamma_N$ are the maps between zero objects.

Consequently, for a locally closed immersion factored as $a=i\circ u:S\hookrightarrow\overline S\hookrightarrow T$ with $u$ open and $i$ closed, put $a_!=i_*u_!$. For its base change $a'=i'\circ u'$ and projection $h_S:S\times_TT'\to S$, the composite of $\gamma^{-1}$ and $\beta$ gives a natural isomorphism
$$a'_!h_S^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}h^*a_!M\qquad(M\in D^b(S,R_S)).$$
No constructibility or derived-completeness hypothesis is imposed on these bounded inputs.

proof.text: Obtain quasi-compactness of each displayed open from QuasiCompact.of_comp and the Over commutativity relation; this uses finite type hypotheses only to form a complementary open in the locally closed argument, where Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian applies. Ranges after base change are complementary by Scheme.image_preimage_eq_of_isPullback applied to the whole source. The assumed open and closed immersion instances already give their permanence hypotheses.

Apply condensed_open_closed_recollement with arbitrary condensed coefficients to extract exactness and full faithfulness of the underived closed direct image. Its counit is therefore invertible. The module open extension is fully faithful by linearization of the fully faithful sheaf open extension and the coefficient scalar equivalence. Exact-derived adjunctions preserve these unit and counit isomorphisms.

For a cartesian open square, use profinitePointModuleForgetPullbackIso and the sheaf openImmersionLowerShriekBaseChangeIso to see that the pullback of an open extension lies in the essential image of the primed module open extension. The primed counit on it is invertible. Apply this counit termwise, descend its natural isomorphism by mapDerivedCategoryNatIso, and transport along mapDerivedCategoryCompIso. Thus all three factors of the actual open exchange mate are invertible on every unbounded input. The abelian sheaf base-change API used here is proved in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.FiniteCoefficient.LowerShriek.Open.BaseChange, without a finite coefficient hypothesis; the separate finite-ring wrapper node lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change is not used.

Use the existing module open/closed detection API and its exact-derived lift. The mixed restriction of an open extension vanishes on disjoint ranges. The other mixed restriction follows by applying successively the open and closed adjunction Hom equivalences to the identity, then descends through homology. For the closed mate, its open restriction is between zero objects using the pullback square comparison, and its closed restriction is invertible by the counit identity from the adjunction Hom bijection. Joint reflection makes the closed mate invertible. The same Hom bijection gives the displayed open unit identity. Specifically use CondensedRing.jointlyReflectIsomorphisms_upperStar_of_isCompl and Functor.jointlyReflectIsomorphisms_pairFunctor_mapDerivedCategory, proved source-library APIs on module objects; this does not invoke the separate ringed-module detection theorem.

Whisker the actual unbounded open and closed mate isomorphisms by the bounded inclusion. Exact-functor homology comparisons preserve the bounded predicate for every functor used. Supply both mixed zero objects and uniqueness of their zero morphism, together with the actual unit/counit normalizations proved above.

For a locally closed factorization, form an actual open complement to the closed image on the ambient scheme; locally Noetherianity makes this open quasi-compact. Pull it back to the primed ambient scheme. Apply the preceding closed-mate argument to this pair and the open-mate argument to the given open square. Whisker the open mate by the primed closed direct image, associate the functors, and compose with the inverse closed mate. Whisker by the bounded inclusion. Exactness gives both output bounds, and the inverse identity proves the displayed cancellation equation.
